title: wallet+lender-boa+closing: least-privilege grant scoping (read-only container, writes to dedicated resources)
description: roborev sm-28 HIGH #1/#3 (codex + claude-security): the wallet's container grant materialises Write with acl:default on /mortgage/, so a write-granted lender's service identity can modify ANY member (credentials, anchors) and the closing party's Control lets it rewrite /mortgage/.acl wholesale — bypassing the app-level revocation invariant (WAC is the real enforcement). sm-28 ALREADY closed the receipt-integrity portion structurally (protected /mortgage/receipts/ subcontainer with an owner+service-only ACL overriding the container default; policy history reads only there; display ledger tolerant). The RESIDUAL is credential/anchor write-exposure + container-Control. Correct fix is cross-surface: (a) protect /mortgage/credentials/ + /mortgage/zk/ with read-only-for-parties ACLs the wallet sets; (b) move lender write-back (currently /mortgage/application + /mortgage/decision — RESOURCE_POD_PATHS, lender-boa/lib/server/loan.ts) into a dedicated writable output subcontainer and grant Write only there; (c) grant closing Control ONLY on the closing-record resource ACL, not the container. Touches wallet (grant modeling), lender-boa (write paths), closing (ACL management). Acceptance: negative tests prove a write-granted party cannot modify credentials/anchors nor rewrite the container ACL.

title: sm-34-fix: closing app production hardening (roborev High/Med)
description:
Address roborev findings on PR #22 (sm-34 closing app):
HIGH 1 - apps/closing/app/closing-experience.tsx:56 client requests send no Authorization/DPoP headers so real scene endpoints fail auth (Playwright hides this by intercepting requests); use authenticated Solid-OIDC fetch + integration test against real handlers.
HIGH 2 - apps/closing/lib/server/pod-rail.ts:86 services default to anonymousPodFetch so authenticated calls cannot read/write private WAC-protected pod resources; supply grant-authenticated service fetch (sm-28 seam).
HIGH 3 - apps/closing/lib/server/scene.ts:184 repeating close overwrites the closing record and unconditionally regrants lender access; after revocation a reload silently regrants with no receipt. Make close idempotent/immutable (409 on existing) and never regrant on repeat.
MED 4 - apps/closing/lib/server/scene.ts:200 ACL is mutated before the receipt is written; a failed receipt write changes access with no ledger record. Implement recoverable transition (pending/committed receipt or ACL compensation).
LOW 5 - packages/ui/src/app-shell.tsx:45 skip link targets #main-content but wallet/tour/lender consumers do not provide that id; have AppShell own the target wrapper or require the id across consumers.
notes:
SUPERSEDED by the in-flight Fable fix on bead/sm-34 (PR #22) — these are NOT optional demo-hardening: finding #3 (repeat-close silently regrants revoked lender access) is a real security bug that breaks scene 5's control thesis, and the e2e mocked the auth path so green tests didn't prove it. The Fable agent is fixing all 3 High + Med with real-auth e2e + an immutable-revocation regression test, gated on a clean claude-security verdict before merge. Close this when PR #22 merges clean.

RESOLVED on PR #22 head 8bfadac (6 review rounds): all 3 High + 1 Med + follow-on findings fixed; e2e mocking REMOVED (real DPoP auth end-to-end, property recipe); closing service identity = solid-kit createServicePodFetch (client_credentials+DPoP), no anonymous fallback (503 fail-closed); revocation immutable + regression-tested via real WAC reads at unit/route/e2e; receipt/ACL consistency with compensation+repair+collision validation; per-pod in-process serialization (sm-9kz tracks shared lock). VERDICTS on 8bfadac: codex clean + claude-security clean (3 consecutive clean security rounds). PR CI green (incl. e2e) since 3c8a207; Vercel deploy green. Close when PR #22 merges.

title: solid-vc upstream: typed-literal claim support (xsd:date) in the structured issue path
description: Why: the pinned @jeswr/solid-vc lowers credentialSubject claims from JSON (writeClaim) and cannot emit datatyped literals like xsd:date, which the sm-19 employment/appraisal/title shapes REQUIRE (schema:startDate, dcterms:issued, mort:searchedThrough). vc-kit therefore signs/verifies claim QUADS through the documented ProofSuite seam (packages/vc-kit/src/credential.ts documents the rationale). Upstream fix: writeClaim support for a typed-literal form (e.g. {'@value','@type'}) plus (optionally) exporting GraphBuilder; then verifyCredential's credentialToRdf(unsigned(vc)) round-trip can express these graphs and vc-kit could migrate to the structured path. jeswr-owned repo (PR in-scope per AGENTS.md convention 7) but requires mirror re-publish + pin bump in remoteGitAllow + packages/vc-kit. Acceptance: solid-vc issue()+verifyCredential() round-trips a credential with an xsd:date subject claim; vc-kit pin bumped; vc-kit either migrates or documents why the quad path stays.

title: wallet: cross-instance receipt-store reconciliation (readiness sentinel / shared lock)
description: roborev sm-28 round-7: the RECEIPT-STORE integrity races are now CLOSED at runtime by a readiness sentinel (apps/wallet/lib/grants/engine.ts READY_SENTINEL) — no shared lock needed, landed in sm-28. The store is marked ready ONLY after provision+lock+reconcile-clean; any transition on a locked-but-unmarked store fails closed (retryable 409). This closes: (a) the failed-reconcile retry-laundering (reachable SINGLE-instance via a transient DELETE-failure + one retry — round-6 mis-scoped it as cross-instance-only; corrected) and (b) the concurrent-instance legitimate-receipt misclassification, plus sweeps the nested-container-plant DoS into ordinary fail-closed. Regression: receipt-store-window.test.ts 'failed reconcile never marks ready, retry fails closed'. REMAINING scope of THIS bead: fold the sentinel into the GENERAL cross-instance transition lock (grant racing revoke across instances) — i.e. sm-9kz — so the whole rail (not just the receipt store) is multi-instance-safe. Lower priority now that the security-relevant receipt-store races are closed.

title: wallet/data-model: sign wallet consent receipts (cryptographic policy-record integrity)
description: roborev sm-28 round-3 residual: the /mortgage/receipts/ protected store + tamper-checked lock stops every NON-Control party from forging policy records, but a party holding acl:Control on /mortgage/ (the closing party, or any non-wallet Control grant) could pre-create the store, plant SHACL-valid forged receipts at deterministic vault IRIs, and install a matching owner+service-only lock — the wallet then trusts a frozen forged snapshot. WAC alone cannot prove a receipt was WALLET-written. Structural closure: sign wallet consent receipts (buildConsentReceipt → eddsa-rdfc-2022 via vc-kit issue path, wallet service key) and have readPolicyHistory verify the signature + issuer == wallet service before trusting a record for immutability/sequence. Complements the cross-surface least-privilege bead (remove closing's container Control). Until then the container-Control forge path is the documented residual; the demo's per-visitor Mode-1 pods + wallet-mediated Mode-2 flow (store always wallet-created first, before any party grant) do not reach it. Acceptance: a forged-but-unsigned policy record is ignored even inside a matching lock; regression test with a Control-holding attacker.

title: solid-api-auth: allowInsecureLoopback must relax the https WebID-claim rule (loopback dev identities cannot verify)
description: Found in sm-22: @jeswr/solid-api-auth's DpopApiVerifier.extractWebId hard-requires https: WebID claims even with allowInsecureLoopback=true, although that option's doc says it allows 'loopback-HTTP issuers + WebID hosts (dev/CI only)'. Result: a loopback-http dev identity (harness pattern, http://localhost:<port>/profile#me) can NEVER pass verification; solid-kit's dev issuer works around it by minting https-schemed WebIDs plus a TLS-strip profileFetch/webidFetch seam (packages/solid-kit/src/auth/dev-issuer.ts). Fix belongs upstream in jeswr/solid-api-auth (Jesse-owned, PR in-scope): accept a loopback-http webid claim iff allowInsecureLoopback (mirror solid-auth-core validateWebId), gate + new dist, then repin in solid-kit and drop the dev-issuer TLS-strip seam + test seams. Acceptance: solid-kit auth tests pass with a plain http loopback WebID and no profileFetch injection.

title: solid-sdk/solid-vc: browser-safe Bitstring status-list codec
description: solid-vc's encode/decodeStatusList uses node:zlib gzipSync/gunzipSync and Buffer base64url — both break under bundler browser polyfills (browserify-zlib rejects Uint8Array input; feross/buffer lacks base64url). The wallet (sm-28) carries scoped workarounds: a Buffer base64url patch (apps/wallet/lib/pod/buffer-base64url-patch.ts) and passing a Buffer-typed bitstring into StatusListClient.create. Upstream fix in jeswr/solid-vc: feature-detect (CompressionStream/DecompressionStream or pako fallback) + manual base64url codec; then drop the wallet patches. Jesse's repo — PR in-scope after lead approval.

title: issuer apps: rehydrate StatusIndexAllocator occupancy on restart
description: Why: vc-kit's StatusIndexAllocator is in-memory; an issuer app (verifications sm-29, property sm-33, gse sm-32) that restarts must rebuild occupancy or risk allocating an index already carried by a live credential (deriveStatusIndex is deterministic per seed, so same-seed reallocation is safe, but DIFFERENT credentials could probe into a lost index). vc-kit exposes reserve() for exactly this. Acceptance: each issuer app rebuilds allocator state on boot from its issued-credentials container (or persists allocations beside the list) before issuing; collision test covering restart.

title: lender-boa: wire the grant-authenticated lender service identity into the podIoFetch seam
description: Decision 0015 L4 consuming side is stubbed: lib/server/pod.ts pod IO defaults to an ANONYMOUS redirect-refusing fetch, proven (test/pod-auth.test.ts WAC suite) to fail closed against WAC pods. Once sm-28 lands the ODRL/DPV grant pipeline (WAC materialised for the lender WebID) + the lender's client-credential DPoP identity, inject that identity's fetch via the podIoFetch seam and extend the WAC test to prove the GRANTED read succeeds while the ungranted one still fails. SECURITY (roborev security job 5579, Low): the L2 backward acknowledgment assumes <pod>profile/card is owner-only-writable; once the lender fetch is PRIVILEGED, a forged acknowledgment on an allowlisted host permitting non-owner card writes would channel privileged IO into a victim's pod — when implementing, bind via the grant registry instead of the card where a grant exists, or add a fail-closed check/test that acknowledgment cards on allowlisted origins are not anonymously writable. Acceptance: pod-rail service constructs the lender service fetch from env (fail-closed when unset in Mode 2), happy+denied grant tests against the oidc harness, acknowledgment-writability guard or grant-registry binding with test, README limitation bullet removed.

title: vc-kit Tier B: size-limit manifest response body before JSON.parse
description: roborev flagged (sm-25, job 5536) that loadProofManifest reads response.json() fully before the sub-proof/count/byte bounds apply, so a hostile pod could allocate a large JSON body first. DOS-class (out of scope for the sm-25 security bar; Tier B verified:true is documented non-authorization and the security review cleared it), but worth a bounded streaming reader that treats Content-Length as an early-rejection hint and caps total bytes before JSON.parse. Acceptance: loadProofManifest rejects a body over a configurable cap without fully buffering it; test with an oversized stub response.

title: vc-kit: status-list pod resource is opaque vc+ld+json — revisit RDF-native hosting
description: Why: the hosted BitstringStatusListCredential is PUT as application/vc+ld+json because the SSRF-guarded pod (correctly) refuses application/ld+json carrying the remote VC 2.0 @context, so the list is stored byte-exact/opaque rather than as queryable pod RDF (packages/vc-kit/src/status.ts LIST_CONTENT_TYPE comment). Verifiers consume it as JSON per the W3C spec, so nothing is broken - this is an RDF-discipline nicety. Options: pinned-context allowlist in the sparq server for https://www.w3.org/ns/credentials/v2 (upstream, log in docs/research/lws-gaps.md), or an inline-context serialisation. Acceptance: decision recorded (or lws-gaps entry filed); if implemented, the hosted list parses as RDF on the pod AND still passes solid-vc's resolveBitstringStatus id/purpose/signature checks.
